LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it necessary to read a text fluently? 3. How does fluency affect the meaning of the content read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. preview a text and make predictions about

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. preview a text and make predictions about

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a text and practise the following: previewing, predicting, scanning), 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination as the learner looks for better ways of doing a task as they predict what a text is about by

looking at the title and images.

● Learning to learn as the learner reads independently and makes use of signal words such as connectors and

conjunctions in a text.

12

Values:
● Responsibility is promoted as the learner offers leadership and guidance as they jointly determine how words in a text

are used together to enhance meanings.

● Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates diverse opinions as they watch a recording and discuss the accuracy,

speed and expressiveness of the reader.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship as learners inculcate ethnic and social relations as they collaboratively look at the text title and images to

predict what the text is about.

Suggested Learning Resources: Dictionaries, resource persons, audio recordings, adapted digital devices with filter

keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand. universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces,

weighted pencil/pen grips
